headline: US bitcoin funds are on course for their worst month on record, while bitcoin holds near $60,500 in thin Thanksgiving trading ahead of Friday's roughly $7 billion options expiry.

market.asOf: Read from CoinMarketCap at about 19:52 UTC on Thu 26 Nov (02:52 Bangkok Fri 27 Nov). Blockchain.com showed bitcoin at about $60,550 at the same time. Use the live prices on this page.
market.fearGreed: 9 out of 100 on CoinMarketCap's Fear and Greed Index; Alternative.me's index showed 11, which it labels "Extreme Fear". Read about 20:15 UTC Thu 26 Nov.

stories.title: US bitcoin funds head for their worst month since they launched
stories.summary: Money has left US spot bitcoin funds for seven trading days in a row, and November's withdrawals are already the biggest of any month since the funds launched in January 2024. US markets were shut for Thanksgiving on Thursday, so the next daily flow figures come after Friday's half-day session.
points: US spot bitcoin funds lost a net $453.1 million on Wed 25 Nov, the seventh straight day of outflows; BlackRock's IBIT accounted for $329.7 million, per The Block.
November outflows total about $5.39 billion so far, about 20% more than the previous record of $4.51 billion in June 2026, per CoinDesk.

The funds are about $5.02 billion in the red for 2026, after inflows of $35.24 billion in their first year and $21.37 billion in 2025, per CoinDesk. A negative 2026 would be their first year of net outflows.
US spot ether funds lost $68.5 million on Wednesday, their ninth straight outflow day, and about $1.3 billion so far in November, per The Block.

stories.title: Bitcoin holds near $60,500 on a quiet Thanksgiving, with $7 billion of options expiring Friday
stories.summary: Bitcoin kept most of its bounce from Wednesday's low while US stock markets were closed, and traders betting on a fall took most of the forced selling. A closely watched chart signal turned negative, and the biggest bets for Friday's options expiry are protection against further drops.
points: Bitcoin was about $60,560 around 1pm ET on Thursday, up 1.39% on the day and down 3.67% on the week, per Decrypt.

On Bitstamp, bitcoin fell to $57,209 on Wednesday and reached $61,509 on Thursday, per Bitcoin.com News; liquidations across the crypto market were under $313 million, and 75% ($237 million) were bets on a fall, per CoinGlass data it cites.
Bitcoin's 50-day exponential moving average ($71,478) fell below its 200-day one ($74,516), a pattern chartists call a "death cross", per Decrypt.
About $7 billion of bitcoin options and $0.6 billion of ether options expire on Deribit on Friday 27 Nov; the put/call ratio for that expiry is 0.89, per CoinDesk.
Galaxy's Alex Thorn is watching a $58,525 daily close and a $59,517 weekly close, the June lows, per CoinDesk.

stories.title: JPMorgan reads Strategy's record-low premium as a sign of bitcoin 'capitulation', as long-held coins stay put
stories.summary: JPMorgan analysts say Strategy (MSTR), the biggest corporate bitcoin holder, now trades below the value of its bitcoin, a record low they read as capitulation (sellers giving up). Separately, Glassnode data shows a rising share of bitcoin that has not moved for a year or more. These are analysts' readings, not forecasts.
points: Strategy's mNAV, its market value divided by the value of its bitcoin, fell to about 0.88x, a new record low, per The Block citing JPMorgan.
JPMorgan puts bitcoin's production cost at about $86,000, which could pressure higher-cost miners while bitcoin trades near $60,000, per The Block.
Bitcoin left unmoved for at least a year is 68.5% of supply, up from 62% in July, per CoinDesk citing Glassnode; CoinDesk notes the pattern says little about timing.

briefs.title: KuCoin to delist Monero
briefs.summary: KuCoin will remove its four Monero (XMR) pairs on 30 Nov at 08:00 UTC; XMR fell about 15% to a $436 low within roughly 4 hours, per U.Today.

briefs.title: UK regulator plans tougher DeFi rules
briefs.summary: The FCA plans to require DeFi platforms to be authorized and to bar UK-regulated exchanges from sending retail trades to DeFi; final guidance is due January 2027, per Decrypt.

briefs.title: US bitcoin reserve bill reaches the full House
briefs.summary: H.R. 8957 would bar selling the government's reserve bitcoin for 20 years; The Block says its odds are slim before this Congress ends, and Polymarket gives a national reserve by year-end 4%.

briefs.title: Europe's only spot bitcoin ETF starts trading in Switzerland
briefs.summary: BIT's BBIT listed on SIX Swiss Exchange with 350 BTC and a 0.19% fee; it is offered only in Switzerland, per The Block.

briefs.title: Two funds value Ripple shares about 70% apart
briefs.summary: SEC filings show one fund marked Ripple at about $90 a share and another at $300 as of 30 Sept, per CoinDesk.

calendar.event: Deribit monthly bitcoin and ether options expiry
calendar.note: About $7 billion of bitcoin options and $0.6 billion of ether options expire, put/call ratio 0.89, with large put bets at $60,000, $58,000, $50,000 and $40,000, per CoinDesk. Bitcoinist gives $6.92 billion and a "max pain" level of $71,000.

calendar.event: US stock markets close early after Thanksgiving
calendar.note: Stocks close at 1:00pm ET, per NYSE; SIFMA recommends a 2:00pm ET early close for US bond markets.

calendar.event: Binance Blockchain Week, Bangkok; Fed quiet period begins
calendar.note: At the Queen Sirikit National Convention Center, per Khaosod English. The Fed's pre-meeting blackout runs from Sat 28 Nov to Thu 10 Dec, per the St. Louis Fed.

calendar.event: Trump Media (DJT) noteholders can demand repayment
calendar.note: Holders of its convertible notes due 2028 can require the company to buy them back for cash; about $883.5 million is outstanding after a $100 million buyback, per StockTitan.

calendar.event: MSCI removes Strategy (MSTR) from its indexes
calendar.note: Takes effect after the close on 30 Nov. MSCI-linked funds hold about 13 million MSTR shares, about 3.1% of the total; JPMorgan estimated about $2.8 billion of selling, per Cointelegraph.

calendar.event: ISM manufacturing PMI (Nov), job openings (JOLTS, Oct); Fed's Bowman testifies to the House
calendar.note: ISM: October was 55.5, per ISM. JOLTS: September was about 7.5 million, per the BLS; Nowflation lists 7.3 million expected. Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman appears at the House Financial Services "Oversight of Prudential Regulators" hearing, per the Fed's calendar.
October was +86,000, per Fox Business. Salesforce holds its earnings webcast at 5:00pm ET.
October was 54.5, below the 54.8 expected, per InvestingLive. Weekly jobless claims are also due, per Nowflation.
Forecasts differ: Nowflation lists +82,000 jobs and 4.2% unemployment; Continuum Economics expects +95,000 and 4.1%. October payrolls rose 165,000 with unemployment at 4.1%, per Continuum Economics.
Markets expect a rate hike, not a cut: CME FedWatch put the chance of a quarter-point hike at 97.8% on 25 Nov, per MarketSpeaker. Press conference at 2:30pm ET, per the Fed's calendar.
